sunline-crank-fc.seoTitle: Sunline Crank FC Diameter & Reel Capacity | ReelCalc
sunline-crank-fc.metaDescription: Compare verified Sunline Crank FC diameters and package lengths. Estimate reel capacity, choose a working fill, and plan backing from exact specifications.
sunline-crank-fc.quickSummary: Crank FC is Sunline's reaction-bait fluorocarbon, designed with additional stretch for crankbaits and related moving lures. The US range has five strengths from 8 to 16 lb, each in 200- and 660-yard packages. It is a different formulation from FC Sniper, not a crankbait label applied to the same chart.
sunline-crank-fc.suitabilityTitle: Is Crank FC right for your setup?
sunline-crank-fc.suitabilitySummary: Consider Crank FC when fluorocarbon suits your crankbait, jerkbait, or other reaction-lure setup. Its intended cushioning is a design claim, not a measured stretch result here. Diameter and usable casting reserve still matter when selecting a strength for a particular reel.
strengthGuide: The 10 lb entry is .260 mm; 14 lb is .310 mm. Recalculate the fill when moving between them instead of assuming the extra four pounds leave capacity unchanged.
This is an 8-16 lb range. A heavier lure or cover requirement outside that range calls for a different verified line, not an invented Crank FC strength.
The 8 lb option at .235 mm can conserve spool space, but this calculator does not predict crankbait running depth or whether a chosen rod and lure can tolerate that strength.

spoolingGuide.title: Filler or bulk
spoolingGuide.text: All five verified strengths offer 200 and 660 yards. A 660-yard package is a bulk supply, not an instruction to fill a reel with all of it.

spoolingGuide.title: Keep casting reserve
spoolingGuide.text: For repeated long casts, allow for trimmed and retied sections when choosing a working length over backing. Replenish the working section before the connection enters ordinary casts.

spoolingGuide.title: Check the product name
spoolingGuide.text: Crank FC, FC Sniper, and Dostrike FC have different product identities. Use the diameter for the exact line being wound.

faqs.question: Is Crank FC nylon?
faqs.answer: No. Sunline identifies it as 100% fluorocarbon. The additional-stretch positioning does not change its material.

faqs.question: Does this chart cover only 10, 12, and 14 lb?
faqs.answer: No. The current manufacturer chart also verifies 8 and 16 lb, and both package lengths are listed for every strength.

faqs.question: Will a thinner strength make my crankbait dive farther?
faqs.answer: This page calculates spool capacity, not lure depth. Lure design, cast length, retrieve, and tackle choices also affect the presentation.

xbraid-x9-fulldrag-braid.seoTitle: XBraid X9 Fulldrag Diameter & Reel Capacity | ReelCalc
xbraid-x9-fulldrag-braid.metaDescription: Compare verified XBraid X9 Fulldrag diameters and package lengths. Estimate reel capacity, choose a working fill, and plan backing from exact specifications.
xbraid-x9-fulldrag-braid.construction: Eight woven strands around one core; nine-strand braid
xbraid-x9-fulldrag-braid.quickSummary: X9 Fulldrag uses eight strands around a ninth core. The US Multi Color SKU range verified here supplies 8-120 lb labels, with package length changing by strength. Its depth-and-distance color system and central-core construction distinguish it from an ordinary eight-strand XBraid.
xbraid-x9-fulldrag-braid.suitabilityTitle: Is X9 Fulldrag right for your setup?
xbraid-x9-fulldrag-braid.suitabilitySummary: Consider Fulldrag when you want a multicolor braided mainline and a clearly identified working length. The core is a construction feature, not evidence that line can never flatten or fail. For offshore use, plan depth, current-induced line angle, fish runs, and retying reserve before choosing backing.
strengthGuide: The official Multi Color 15 lb diameter is .008 inch / .19 mm, and 20 lb is .009 inch / .23 mm. These are the exact distributor SKU rows, not the different metric values found in a retailer chart.
The 65 lb entry retains 165-, 330-, 660-, and 3,300-yard packages. At 80 lb and above, this verified set starts at 330 yards.
The 100 and 120 lb labels are genuine entries, at .50 and .55 mm. They must not be attached to an existing lighter-strength ID just to preserve an old selector.

spoolingGuide.title: Use the Multi Color range
spoolingGuide.text: The verified SKUs end in ML. Marsh Green appears separately in the distributor data but has blank diameter cells, so it is not silently assigned Multi Color values.

spoolingGuide.title: Choose reserve for the application
spoolingGuide.text: A jig dropped deep or allowed to drift uses more line than the water depth alone. Keep sufficient working line above the backing connection for that use and expected runs.

spoolingGuide.title: Treat colors as a reference
spoolingGuide.text: Color changes help track paid-out line, but knots and removed sections interrupt the original sequence. They do not replace a check of available working length.

faqs.question: Does X9 mean nine woven carriers?
faqs.answer: The manufacturer describes eight strands woven around a ninth core. This guide keeps that construction distinction explicit.

faqs.question: Is 165 yards offered at 120 lb?
faqs.answer: Not in the verified Multi Color rows. The 120 lb packages listed here are 330, 660, and 3,300 yards.

faqs.question: Why not use the first retailer diameter chart?
faqs.answer: Some discovered retailer values differ at 15 and 20 lb. This page uses exact official distributor ML SKU evidence and records the discrepancy.

sunline-shooter-bms-azayaka-ny.metaDescription: Compare verified Sunline BMS Azayaka NY diameters and package lengths. Estimate reel capacity, choose a working fill, and plan backing from exact specifications.
sunline-shooter-bms-azayaka-ny.construction: Nylon monofilament; two-meter Bite Marker System
sunline-shooter-bms-azayaka-ny.quickSummary: Shooter BMS Azayaka NY is the nylon member of Sunline's marked-line family. The current Japanese product uses a silk-white base with yellow-green, orange, and black markings in a two-meter cycle. Its 80-meter package is about 87.49 yards, not 80 yards and not the FC model's bulk option.
sunline-shooter-bms-azayaka-ny.suitabilityTitle: Is BMS Azayaka NY right for your setup?
sunline-shooter-bms-azayaka-ny.suitabilitySummary: Consider this line when watching a marked nylon mainline is part of your reaction-bait or topwater presentation. The visibility system is a product feature; it cannot guarantee bite detection. Plan the relatively short package against casting distance and future trimming before deciding on backing.
strengthGuide: The product-specific 5 lb entry is .190 mm. Do not replace it with .185 mm from a generic size chart: the exact NY product table is the evidence here.
At 10 lb the standard diameter is .260 mm; 20 lb is .370 mm. The package remains 80 meters as strength rises, but reel capacity does not.
NY means nylon. BMS Azayaka FC is fluorocarbon with a different marking cycle and package range; sharing a family name does not make its data interchangeable.

spoolingGuide.title: Budget the 80 meters
spoolingGuide.text: A complete package provides about 87.49 yards before losses to knots and trimming. A long cast can consume a substantial part of that amount; check your required reserve first.

spoolingGuide.title: Use markings with context
spoolingGuide.text: The repeating two-meter color system aids observation. It is not a calibrated measurement of remaining spool capacity after pieces have been removed.

spoolingGuide.title: Keep the right suffix
spoolingGuide.text: Check NY on the package before winding. The FC product is a separate fluorocarbon, not another color of this nylon line.

faqs.question: Can I select the 320-meter FC bulk spool for NY?
faqs.answer: No. The verified NY product lists an 80-meter package. The FC model's bulk size is not evidence for NY.

faqs.question: Are the pound labels breaking-strength guarantees?
faqs.answer: Sunline labels the values as reference strength in the Japanese product table. Actual results depend on conditions and knots.

faqs.question: Where do the inch values come from?
faqs.answer: They are explicit conversions of Sunline's product-specific standard millimeter diameters. They are not separately measured or published inch values.

sufix-832-advanced-superline.metaDescription: Check verified Sufix 832 Advanced Superline diameters and strength-specific packages. Plan a full reel fill or a working length over backing with the exact line diameter.
sufix-832-advanced-superline.quickSummary: 832 combines seven HMPE fibers with one GORE Performance Fiber. The name refers to eight fibers and 32 weaves per inch. This is the U.S. Advanced Superline mainline, not 832 Ice Braid or the lead-core trolling product.
sufix-832-advanced-superline.construction: Eight fibers: seven HMPE fibers and one GORE Performance Fiber; 32 weaves per inch
sufix-832-advanced-superline.suitabilityTitle: Is 832 Advanced Superline right for your setup?
sufix-832-advanced-superline.suitabilitySummary: Consider 832 when you want braid for the working line and a choice of short filler or large bulk packages. Its broad strength range does not make every size suitable for every reel: choose the rod and presentation first. A thin spinning setup may need substantial backing, while a heavier casting setup may consume most of a 150-yard package.
strengthGuide: The 10 and 15 lb rows are 0.008 and 0.0085 inch respectively. Keep that fourth decimal when comparing capacity; displaying both as 0.008 would hide a real difference in the manufacturer chart.
The 30-65 lb sizes occupy progressively more spool volume. Evaluate the lure, cover, hook wire and rod rating before stepping up; a larger pound label alone is not a setup recommendation.
The 100 and 130 lb products have different package options from the lighter fillers. Do not apply the 150-yard default to those strengths.

spoolingGuide.title: Pick a working length before a bulk spool
spoolingGuide.text: Compare a 150-yard working section against the selected reel capacity. Leave room for casts, runs and future trimming. If the reel holds substantially more, sound mono backing can occupy the unused volume.

spoolingGuide.title: Keep the diameter precise
spoolingGuide.text: The 15 lb row is published at 0.0085 inch. The calculator should use that exact input even if a compact chart rounds the displayed value.

spoolingGuide.title: Separate the bite section
spoolingGuide.text: A leader connects to the lure end of 832; backing belongs beneath it. Select any leader for the cover and presentation, then calculate spool capacity with the 832 mainline diameter.

faqs.question: What does 832 mean?
faqs.answer: Sufix specifies eight fibers and 32 weaves per inch, with seven HMPE fibers and one GORE Performance Fiber.

faqs.question: Is 832 Advanced Lead Core the same product?
faqs.answer: No. The lead-core trolling line and 832 Ice Braid are separately specified products. This chart is only for Advanced Superline.

faqs.question: Can I buy every strength in 150 yards?
faqs.answer: No. The verified 100 and 130 lb entries use 1,200- and 3,000-yard packages. Check the selected strength rather than treating all package sizes as universal.

faqs.question: How much 832 Advanced Superline will fit my reel?
faqs.answer: Use the exact strength and the reel's published capacity. Pound test is not a fixed diameter, so equal-strength products can produce different fill estimates.

faqs.question: Is one 150-yard package enough?
faqs.answer: Only when it covers the planned working length and an appropriate reserve. Backing can fill unused volume, but cannot supply more working line for long casts, deep drops or fish runs.

sufix-promix-braid.metaDescription: Check verified Sufix ProMix Braid diameters and strength-specific packages. Plan a full reel fill or a working length over backing with the exact line diameter.
sufix-promix-braid.quickSummary: ProMix Braid is Sufix's HMPE mainline with a color-retention-focused Color Injection process. It is distinct from ProMix monofilament. The U.S. braid chart includes 6 lb, then 10-80 lb; there is no verified 8 lb row.
sufix-promix-braid.construction: Densely woven HMPE braid with Sufix Color Injection processing
sufix-promix-braid.suitabilityTitle: Is ProMix Braid right for your setup?
sufix-promix-braid.suitabilitySummary: ProMix Braid suits an angler comparing a general-purpose braid for fresh or salt water who wants to plan a practical working fill. Sufix emphasizes color retention, but that is not a measured service-life promise from ReelCalc. Choose a visible or subdued color for your own line-watching needs and check the package offered in that exact strength and color.
strengthGuide: For the smallest verified size, 6 lb, the current variants support 150 and 300 yards. The larger bulk lengths begin at 10 lb; do not buy by the page-wide package list alone.
The 15 lb row is 0.0085 inch, between the 10 lb row at 0.008 and 20 lb at 0.009. Those differences matter more to spool volume than the ProMix name.
The 40-80 lb options need a suitable rod and reel for heavier fishing. A capacity result is not proof that a compact reel or light rod is appropriate for that strength.

spoolingGuide.title: Choose filler or bulk by demand
spoolingGuide.text: A 150-yard package can supply a working fill over backing. Bulk ProMix makes more sense when the total verified demand across reels exceeds a smaller package, not simply because a large spool appears in the menu.

spoolingGuide.title: Wind a firm braid bed
spoolingGuide.text: Follow the reel instructions for braid attachment, maintain even tension and stop at the recommended fill level. Color retention does not prevent loose winding or braid slipping on an unsuitable arbor.

spoolingGuide.title: Do not substitute ProMix mono
spoolingGuide.text: ProMix monofilament is a separate Sufix product. The same brand and family name are not enough to identify a diameter for this braid capacity calculation.

sufix-performance-braid.quickSummary: Performance Braid is the Sufix line marketed around Y6 braiding. This source-reviewed U.S. selection uses 100-yard packages in 6, 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 65 and 80 lb. It is not Performance Ice Braid or Performance Lead Core.
sufix-performance-braid.construction: Braided mainline using Sufix Y6 braiding technology
sufix-performance-braid.suitabilityTitle: Is Performance Braid right for your setup?
sufix-performance-braid.suitabilitySummary: The verified 100-yard package is the key planning constraint here. It can provide a short working fill, but it should not be mistaken for enough line for every full reel. Check your longest deployment, a fish-run reserve and allowance for trimming before using backing to make that package fill the spool.
strengthGuide: The current official chart jumps from 10 to 20 lb. Select an offered strength suited to the rod and lure rather than interpolating a 15 lb product that is not in this verified range.
At 20 lb the official diameter is 0.009 inch; at 65 lb it is 0.016. These are separate spool-volume inputs, even when the same 100-yard retail length is offered.
For long casting or deep-water work, capacity alone cannot make a 100-yard working section adequate. Determine deployment and reserve before choosing the fill.

spoolingGuide.title: Treat 100 yards as a package limit
spoolingGuide.text: Enter a working length no longer than the package provides, unless you have a longer independently verified spool. Backing fills volume, but it does not add usable braid for a long cast or run.

spoolingGuide.title: Keep the join below working depth
spoolingGuide.text: When using mono backing, the connection should remain below the line normally deployed. If 100 yards cannot do that with a suitable reserve, this package is not enough for the setup.

The verified 17 and 20 lb rows are 0.016 and 0.018 inch. On a small spinning spool, physical fit does not establish comfortable handling.

spoolingGuide.title: Elite as backing

spoolingGuide.title: Keep fill level conservative

sufix-advance-fluorocarbon.suitabilitySummary: Consider this product when fluorocarbon will be the line you cast and store on the reel. strengthGuide: The 4-8 lb rows run from 0.007 to 0.009 inch. Compare them with the rod rating and presentation before using them on a small spinning reel.
Advance Fluorocarbon 17 lb is listed at 0.015 inch. Castable Invisiline 17 lb is listed at 0.016; the family names and matching strength do not make those capacity inputs interchangeable.
The 20, 25 and 30 lb sizes progressively increase to 0.017, 0.018 and 0.020 inch. Choose a reel and rod suited to the thicker line, not just a mathematically acceptable capacity.

spoolingGuide.title: Plan the 200-yard working supply

gamma-edge-fluorocarbon.seoTitle: Gamma Edge Fluorocarbon Diameter Chart & Reel Capacity | ReelCalc
gamma-edge-fluorocarbon.metaDescription: Compare verified Gamma Edge Fluorocarbon diameters and strength-specific spool lengths, estimate reel capacity, and plan a full fill or a working section over backing.
gamma-edge-fluorocarbon.quickSummary: Gamma Edge is the brand's general-purpose 100% fluorocarbon main line. Its U.S. size labels run from 4 to 25 lb, including 14 and 16 lb, and are distinct from Gamma's separately published actual-break figures. The verified range includes 50-, 100-, 200-, 500- and 1000-yard packages.
gamma-edge-fluorocarbon.suitabilityTitle: Is Edge Fluorocarbon right for your setup?
gamma-edge-fluorocarbon.suitabilitySummary: Consider Edge for a full fluorocarbon setup when you want more strength choices than the finesse-only Touch range. At 0.012 inch, the 10 lb Edge is materially thicker than 9 lb Touch at 0.0105 inch; the nearby strength labels do not make them interchangeable on a small spinning spool. Gamma emphasizes castability and shock resistance, but those are manufacturer claims rather than comparative ReelCalc tests.
strengthGuide: Edge 4, 6 and 8 lb measure 0.008, 0.010 and 0.011 inch. Begin with the rod's line range and the cover, then check capacity; the 6 lb label should not be treated as a universal thin-line size.

The middle steps are 10, 12, 14 and 16 lb. Keep those actual offered sizes when comparing setups instead of substituting a generic 15 lb record. The U.S. size column identifies the product; the actual-break column is not a replacement label.
Edge 20 and 25 lb take appreciably more space at 0.017 and 0.019 inch. Use these only where the rod, reel, lure and cover justify the diameter, not simply to maximize the strength number.

spoolingGuide.title: Choose a working length before the package
spoolingGuide.text: The 50-yard Pony and 100-yard Filler are real Edge packages, but neither guarantees a full reel fill. Include casting distance, fish runs and retying reserve before deciding whether 200 yards or a larger package is appropriate.

spoolingGuide.title: Straight Edge or optional backing
spoolingGuide.text: A continuous Edge fill avoids a buried connection. A shorter fresh working section over sound backing is another option; keep that knot below the line you normally cast and allow for future trimming.

spoolingGuide.title: Separate Edge from Touch and leader stock
spoolingGuide.text: Use Edge's selected diameter for its capacity. Touch is a different finesse product, and Gamma's dedicated Fluorocarbon Leader has a separate size chart and much shorter retail packages.

faqs.question: Is Edge the same as Gamma Touch?
faqs.answer: No. Edge covers 4-25 lb with its own diameters. Touch is a separate finesse fluorocarbon offered in smaller increments; for example, 8 lb Edge is 0.011 inch and 8 lb Touch is 0.0095 inch.

faqs.question: Does the actual-break column change the line size?
faqs.answer: No. Select the stated U.S. size printed for the SKU. Gamma's actual-break values are manufacturer-reported figures, not ReelCalc testing or a guarantee of knot strength.

faqs.question: Is the 50-yard Edge spool enough for main line?
faqs.answer: Only when your planned working section, including reserve, fits within 50 yards. Check the fill rather than treating a small package as a complete reel load.

faqs.question: How much Edge Fluorocarbon fits my reel?
faqs.answer: Use the selected Edge Fluorocarbon diameter with your reel's published capacity. Pound test is a product strength label, not a universal diameter. Stop filling at the reel manufacturer's recommended level.

faqs.question: Does Edge Fluorocarbon require backing?
faqs.answer: Backing is optional for a full mainline fill. It can make sense under a shorter fresh working section, but the connection must stay below normal casting depth with enough reserve for runs and retying.

cast-fishing-co-x12-frog-flip-braid.exampleBackingLabel: Berkley Trilene Big Game 10 lb mono (0.012 in)
cast-fishing-co-x12-frog-flip-braid.reviewNote: This is a source-based specification and setup guide, not a hands-on review or comparative performance test.
cast-fishing-co-x12-frog-flip-braid.quickSummary: A camo 12-strand braid designed specifically for frogging and flipping vegetation. This guide uses the US 150-yard Frog & Flip product: 65 lb at 0.26 mm and 80 lb at 0.30 mm. Regular X12 Casting Braid is a separate product.
cast-fishing-co-x12-frog-flip-braid.suitabilitySummary: X12 Frog & Flip is aimed at heavy-cover bass presentations, not a default upgrade for every spinning reel. Choose between the two tests using the rod, hook, lure and cover. Both are unusually thin relative to their printed test, so a reel may hold much more than the 150-yard working package. That extra volume is a backing decision, not a reason to force a larger fill.
strengthGuide: Compare the verified 65 and 80 lb options as two physical sizes: 0.26 and 0.30 mm. The test label alone is not a spool-capacity measurement.

For frogs, reserve enough working line for the longest intended cast and subsequent line loss. For short flipping presentations, do not interpret a high full-spool estimate as a required purchase quantity.
Use tackle rated for the selected power application. The 65 or 80 lb label is not a recommended drag setting, and thin braid can dig into lower wraps on a baitcaster.
cast-fishing-co-x12-frog-flip-braid.bestFit: The manufacturer targets pads, reeds, mats and other vegetation where heavy-cover presentations dictate the tackle. The camo color and coating are features of this model, not evidence that fish cannot see the line.
cast-fishing-co-x12-frog-flip-braid.tradeoffTitle: Heavy test does not mean thick line
cast-fishing-co-x12-frog-flip-braid.tradeoff: At the published diameters, capacity can be very large even on a bass baitcaster. Use a measured working section over appropriate backing; do not sacrifice even winding tension to squeeze the numerical maximum onto the spool.
cast-fishing-co-x12-frog-flip-braid.chartNote: Only the US Frog & Flip 150-yard variants are included. No regular X12, BFS or Australian meter-spool values are substituted.
cast-fishing-co-x12-frog-flip-braid.diameterNote: Millimeter diameters are printed in the official variant names. Inch values are explicit mm/25.4 conversions; braid packing remains an estimate.

spoolingGuide.title: Plan the 150-yard working section
spoolingGuide.text: Start with the frog cast or flipping depth, expected runs and a retying reserve. The package supplies 150 yards, which can be less than full-spool capacity at these diameters.

spoolingGuide.title: Keep backing below the cast
spoolingGuide.text: Use backing to occupy unused volume and an attachment suited to the reel arbor. Keep the connection buried beneath the line likely to leave the spool during fishing.

spoolingGuide.title: Wind under controlled tension
spoolingGuide.text: Keep wraps even and follow the reel maker's fill clearance. After a heavy load, check for buried wraps before making another hard cast.

cast-fishing-co-x12-frog-flip-braid.reelcalcNote: Use the exact 65 or 80 lb Frog & Flip record with a real reel capacity rating; this specialty line is not a general-purpose wizard recommendation.

manufacturerFacts.label: Verified construction
manufacturerFacts.text: CAST specifies a 12-strand weave, proprietary water-repellent coating and vegetation-oriented camo color.

manufacturerFacts.label: Verified package
manufacturerFacts.text: US variants list 150 yards at 65 or 80 lb.

manufacturerFacts.label: Manufacturer positioning
manufacturerFacts.text: CAST markets this model for frogging and flipping. Casting-distance and guide-noise claims have not been independently tested here.

setupComparison.title: Frog casts or short pitches?
setupComparison.leftText: Set the working length to cover the longest cast plus usable reserve. A 150-yard package is a supply limit, not a full-fill guarantee.
setupComparison.rightText: Choose line test for the vegetation and tackle, then calculate backing from a deliberate working length. Short presentations do not require filling all spare volume with premium braid.

productGuidance: Keep this model separate from regular X12 Casting Braid.
Check the marked 150-yard US package before using the default spool length.
Treat capacity as an estimate affected by winding tension and packing, especially with this thin high-test braid.

faqs.question: Is Frog & Flip the same as regular X12?
faqs.answer: No. These rows belong to the camo Frog & Flip product. Do not transfer diameters or spool lengths from regular X12 Casting Braid.

faqs.question: Does 65 lb mean I should use 65 lb of drag?
faqs.answer: No. Choose drag for the complete tackle system and fishing conditions. The printed line test is not a drag prescription.

faqs.question: Will one 150-yard spool fill my baitcaster?
faqs.answer: It depends on the reel and the chosen 0.26 or 0.30 mm line. Estimate capacity first, then use backing if the intended working section is shorter than full capacity.

faqs.question: Has ReelCalc confirmed longer casts?
faqs.answer: No. The construction and intended techniques are manufacturer information. This page is not an independent casting-distance test.

rhino-hide-camo-braid.reviewNote: This is a source-based specification and setup guide, not a hands-on review or comparative performance test.
rhino-hide-camo-braid.construction: Camo woven braided line; fiber count not specified
rhino-hide-camo-braid.quickSummary: Zebco's Rhino Hide Camo Braid is listed in 200-yard packages from 10 to 50 lb, with Green Camo and Hi-Vis Orange Camo options. The manufacturer describes non-fading fibers; no carrier count is established in the checked product data.
rhino-hide-camo-braid.suitabilitySummary: The green and orange camo versions give different above-water visibility choices within the same checked strength range. Rhino positions the braid for heavy cover, but a 10 lb option and a 50 lb option should not be treated as interchangeable cover tools. Match the test to the rod, lure and fishing before estimating how much of the 200-yard package to use.
strengthGuide: The 10, 15 and 20 lb sizes are thinner than the 30 and 50 lb options. Compare exact diameter against reel capacity instead of treating every 200-yard package as a full fill.
Choose the heavier sizes for a justified tackle and cover requirement, not because a reel has spare spool volume. Baitcaster handling and tightly packed wraps still matter.
Color is a visibility decision. The green and orange child SKUs have matching checked numeric specifications; the camo pattern is not proof of underwater invisibility.
rhino-hide-camo-braid.fitTitle: Camo braid with two visibility choices
rhino-hide-camo-braid.bestFit: A mainline option for anglers who want the Rhino camo pattern and a 200-yard retail package. Manufacturer heavy-cover positioning does not remove the need to size the complete tackle system.
rhino-hide-camo-braid.tradeoffTitle: A package is not a capacity rating
rhino-hide-camo-braid.tradeoff: The thinnest 10 lb and thickest 50 lb options occupy very different spool volumes. Backing may be useful for a short working fill, but the reel maker's attachment and fill guidance still governs.
rhino-hide-camo-braid.chartNote: Official RNB200 child SKUs verify these five tests and 200-yard spools. The parent page heading incorrectly says monofilament; the child names, line-type attributes and product images identify braid.
rhino-hide-camo-braid.diameterNote: Published inch/mm pairs are retained with normal rounding. These are manufacturer specifications, not measured braid packing diameters.

spoolingGuide.title: Check the RNB200 label
spoolingGuide.text: Use the braid package, not the similarly named RNMF330 monofilament. A 200-yard braid spool and 330-yard mono spool are different products.

spoolingGuide.title: Use backing deliberately
spoolingGuide.text: Choose the braid working length before calculating backing. Use an arbor attachment approved for the reel, and keep the connection below the casting section.

spoolingGuide.title: Watch the line while filling
spoolingGuide.text: Even winding tension and correct spool-lip clearance matter more than forcing the estimated maximum onto the reel.

rhino-hide-camo-braid.reelcalcNote: Use official child-SKU diameters and your exact reel; do not substitute the Rhino monofilament row.

manufacturerFacts.text: 10, 15, 20, 30 and 50 lb; 200 yards; Green Camo and Hi-Vis Orange Camo.

setupComparison.title: Green or orange camo?
setupComparison.leftText: Select the lower-visibility color when that suits your fishing. Choose strength and working length independently of color.
setupComparison.rightText: Select a more visible mainline for tracking it above water. Add a separately selected terminal leader where the presentation calls for one.

rhino-hide-camo-monofilament.exampleBackingLabel: Berkley Trilene Big Game 10 lb mono (0.012 in)
rhino-hide-camo-monofilament.reviewNote: This is a source-based specification and setup guide, not a hands-on review or comparative performance test.
rhino-hide-camo-monofilament.quickSummary: Rhino Hide Camo Monofilament is Zebco's Green Camo mono in 330-yard filler spools, with checked options from 6 to 30 lb. It is distinct from the 200-yard Rhino Hide braid.
rhino-hide-camo-monofilament.suitabilitySummary: Choose Rhino Hide mono when a single-strand mainline suits the presentation and you want the Green Camo offering. Test and diameter need to suit the reel as well as the fishing: the 30 lb option is more than twice the listed inch diameter of the 6 lb option. A line fitting by volume does not establish comfortable handling on a small spinning spool.
strengthGuide: Start with the lighter 6-10 lb options only where the rod, lure and target fish justify them. Check spool handling before treating the capacity result as a recommendation.
The 12-20 lb group occupies more volume and is a different choice from fine mono. Choose it for tackle and cover requirements rather than copying a reel's printed capacity test.
At 25-30 lb, the physical diameter matters considerably. Keep these rows separate from Rhino braid of the same test.
rhino-hide-camo-monofilament.fitTitle: One material from reel to lure
rhino-hide-camo-monofilament.bestFit: A full mono fill can keep the system simple without a separate braid-to-leader connection. The Green Camo treatment is a product feature, not a guarantee of invisible line.
rhino-hide-camo-monofilament.tradeoff: A thicker mono can fit a small reel numerically but still be a poor handling choice. Do not increase strength only to consume a 330-yard package.
rhino-hide-camo-monofilament.chartNote: RNMF330 Green Camo child SKUs provide the verified 6-30 lb options, each at 330 yards.
rhino-hide-camo-monofilament.diameterNote: Official attributes publish inches for all tests and mm for 8 and 25 lb. The official 10 lb RNMF330-10GC package additionally prints .286 mm. Other mm values are explicit conversions from inches, not legacy database measurements.

spoolingGuide.title: Check the RNMF330 package
spoolingGuide.text: Confirm mono, strength and the 330-yard label before planning the fill. The similarly named RNB200 braid is not interchangeable.

spoolingGuide.title: Choose full mono or a working section
spoolingGuide.text: A full fill avoids a backing junction. A shorter mono working section can use backing below it when the reel holds more line than needed; keep the connection out of normal casts.

spoolingGuide.title: Stop at the reel's fill limit
spoolingGuide.text: Use steady tension and the recommended spool-lip clearance. Keep unused line for another fill instead of overfilling to finish the package.

rhino-hide-camo-monofilament.reelcalcNote: Estimate with the exact Rhino mono diameter. Similar test labels on braid will not give the same capacity.

manufacturerFacts.text: Each checked strength is supplied as a 330-yard filler spool in Green Camo.

manufacturerFacts.label: Availability caveat
manufacturerFacts.text: The official product data marks launch year 2027; current retail stock has not been confirmed.

setupComparison.title: Full mono or mono over backing?
setupComparison.leftText: Provides an uninterrupted mainline from arbor to terminal tackle. Use the reel capacity estimate to judge whether one 330-yard package is sufficient.
setupComparison.rightText: Retains a chosen length of Rhino mono above a volume-filling base. Keep enough working line that the junction stays below normal casting and fish-run needs.

Check the listed diameter when comparing with Rhino braid or another mono.

faqs.question: Is Rhino Hide mono the same as the braid?
faqs.answer: No. This is RNMF330 monofilament in 330-yard spools. RNB200 is braid in 200-yard spools.

faqs.question: Are all millimeter figures manufacturer measurements?
faqs.answer: No. The checked attributes publish mm for 8 and 25 lb, and the official 10 lb package prints .286 mm. Other mm values are converted from published inches.

faqs.question: Will 330 yards fill two reels?
faqs.answer: Only when their combined planned working fills fit within 330 yards, allowing for waste and knots. Backing can fill unused spool volume; it does not add working-line length.

faqs.question: Does a capacity fit prove 30 lb is suitable?
faqs.answer: No. Rod rating, lure, cover and handling on the reel still determine suitability.

berkley-trilene-big-game.quickSummary: Trilene Big Game is Berkley's heavy-duty nylon mono for anglers who want stretch, substantial line strength, and a large supply for respooling. Its diameter matters as much as its pound-test label: the selected size can be used as a working main line or as backing beneath another line.
berkley-trilene-big-game.suitabilitySummary: Big Game is worth considering for bait fishing, larger freshwater fish, and saltwater applications where nylon's stretch is useful. It also serves as economical backing. On smaller spinning reels, compare the actual diameter before choosing a heavy strength; a line can physically fit but still be awkward to cast.
berkley-trilene-big-game.chartNote: These entries match official US package listings to the same product codes in Berkley's diameter data. Only resolved strengths and package sizes are shown; the conflicting 25 lb listing is omitted.
strengthGuide: The 10 and 12 lb choices are the lighter entries in this chart. Check their diameters against the reel and lure you intend to use instead of assuming they handle like every other brand with the same strength label.

The 15 and 20 lb choices use more spool space and suit setups that can manage thicker nylon. A larger spool, heavier presentation, or bait-fishing application can make more sense than a small finesse spinning reel.

The 30-50 lb entries are substantial main lines. Choose them for a specific heavy-duty setup, not as a default upgrade for ordinary bass fishing. When Big Game is only backing, its diameter determines the length needed beneath your working line.

spoolingGuide.title: Big Game as the main line
spoolingGuide.text: For a full nylon spool, select your strength and use full-spool capacity. The large retail spool is a supply of line, not an instruction to put all of it on the reel.

spoolingGuide.title: Big Game as backing
spoolingGuide.text: This page calculates Big Game as the selected working line. To put Big Game underneath braid instead, open the braid's guide or the main calculator and select Big Game in the backing field.

spoolingGuide.title: Allow for stretch
spoolingGuide.text: Nylon's stretch changes how a rig feels compared with braid. Set the drag for the complete rod, line, and terminal setup; filling the reel does not establish a safe fighting drag.

faqs.question: Can Trilene Big Game be used for braid backing?
faqs.answer: Yes. Use the Big Game strength and diameter as the backing inputs, with your braid selected as the working main line. This page's calculator instead treats the selected Big Game as the main line.

faqs.question: Will a 1,500-yard spool fit on my reel?
faqs.answer: Usually it is a supply for several fills, not a single fill. The calculator estimates what your selected reel holds at the chosen diameter; stop at the reel's specified fill level.

faqs.question: Why is the 25 lb size absent from this chart?
faqs.answer: The available manufacturer diameter listing conflicts with neighboring strengths. That entry is withheld rather than used for a capacity calculation. This does not mean the product is unavailable.

berkley-vanish.imageCaption: Vanish filler-spool package shown. The chart below covers verified bulk-spool specifications.
berkley-vanish.quickSummary: Berkley Vanish is a fluorocarbon main line designed with casting flexibility in mind. Its sinking material makes it a different choice from nylon for a working line. This guide uses the published US bulk-spool strength and diameter pairs, with capacity estimates based on the selected diameter.
berkley-vanish.suitabilitySummary: Vanish can suit subsurface presentations when you want a fluorocarbon working line without relying on a separate braid-to-leader connection. Lighter diameters are easier to manage on small spinning spools. The heavier entries need tackle that can handle thick fluorocarbon; they are not universal spinning-reel recommendations.
berkley-vanish.chartNote: The chart shows the resolved strength, diameter, and package combinations from Berkley's US Vanish bulk-spool listing. The 2,000- and 1,700-yard amounts are retail supplies, not recommended single-reel fills. Filler-spool and leader packages are not implied by this chart.
strengthGuide: The 6-10 lb entries are the lighter diameters shown here. Start with the rod's line rating, your lure, and the cover you fish. Filling a small spinning reel with fluorocarbon requires attention to line twist and the manufacturer's fill level.

The 12-20 lb choices give you a thicker working line for tackle and presentations that can manage it. For the same reel, increasing diameter reduces the available yardage; the calculator makes that tradeoff visible.

The 30-60 lb entries are heavy fluorocarbon choices. They are included because they have published specifications, not because they are recommended for everyday casting on every reel. A short leader and a full working spool are different jobs.

spoolingGuide.title: A supply spool is not a fill target
spoolingGuide.text: A bulk Vanish spool can supply multiple reel fills. Use the estimated full-spool amount as a starting point, then stop at the reel maker's fill level rather than trying to use the whole retail spool.

spoolingGuide.title: Replacing only the working section
spoolingGuide.text: Backing can let you replace a worn working section without discarding every yard on the spool. Leave enough usable Vanish above the backing connection for the casts and runs you expect.

spoolingGuide.title: Keep the main line and leader distinct
spoolingGuide.text: This guide covers Vanish main line. A leader sold in a short spool should be checked against its own label, not assumed to share every diameter or package option shown here.

faqs.question: Is Vanish nylon with a fluorocarbon coating?
faqs.answer: No. Berkley describes this Vanish main line as 100% fluorocarbon. It should not be confused with a fluorocarbon-coated nylon or copolymer line.

faqs.question: Why does the package menu start at 2,000 yards?
faqs.answer: These are the bulk-spool packages whose strength and diameter combinations are documented in the source used for this chart. The calculator returns the amount for your reel, not the whole package.

faqs.question: Does a capacity estimate mean this strength is a good casting choice?
faqs.answer: Not by itself. The calculation estimates spool space. Match the line to the rod, lure, reel, and fishing conditions, especially with the thickest fluorocarbon sizes.

berkley-x9-braid.quickSummary: Berkley X9 uses nine PE carriers and is positioned around a smooth casting feel. Choose the exact US pound-test label here, then compare its published diameter with your reel's capacity. The same brand's overseas strength labels are not automatically interchangeable with these entries.
berkley-x9-braid.suitabilitySummary: X9 is a candidate when a smooth braid main line and sensitivity are priorities. Its lighter sizes need careful spool tension and drag use; thin braid is not automatically the best choice for a baitcaster. Use the thicker options only when the presentation, cover, and tackle call for them.
berkley-x9-braid.chartNote: US strength and package options are matched by exact product code to Berkley's official diameter records. Inch diameters are published values; the millimeter figures are conversions. Retail lengths vary by strength, particularly in the heaviest sizes.
strengthGuide: The 8-15 lb entries are thin working lines. They can make sense on suitable spinning tackle with an appropriately chosen leader, but a fine diameter calls for careful knots, drag settings, and line management.

The 20-40 lb choices cover a wider range of applications. For baitcasting, choose the line around lure weight, cover, and resistance to digging into lower wraps rather than choosing only the highest capacity number.

The 50-100 lb options are for heavier uses that justify their strength and diameter. Compare both the amount your reel can hold and the package you intend to buy; not every large spool contains the same yardage at every strength.

spoolingGuide.title: Secure the braid at the arbor
spoolingGuide.text: Follow the reel maker's instructions for securing braid. Where backing is used, calculate its amount from its actual diameter instead of treating a mono pound test as a braid diameter.

spoolingGuide.title: Keep firm, even tension
spoolingGuide.text: Wind braid under controlled tension and watch the fill level. Loose lower wraps can change the usable fill and encourage the working line to dig in; the estimate cannot measure your winding tension.

spoolingGuide.title: Match the leader to the job
spoolingGuide.text: A leader is selected for the presentation, cover, knots, and target fish. Its pound test does not need to match the braid label, and changing a short leader does not produce a meaningful increase in spool capacity.

faqs.question: What is the difference between X9 and X5?
faqs.answer: X9 uses nine PE carriers; X5 uses five. Berkley emphasizes smooth casting for X9 and strength around cover for X5. Carrier count alone does not establish the capacity, knot strength, or abrasion performance of a particular spool.

faqs.question: Why do some imported X9 packages show different strengths?
faqs.answer: Regional labels can use different strength descriptions. This chart follows the matched US product codes and pound-test labels rather than mapping an overseas number to a US size by name alone.

faqs.question: Will the published diameter guarantee an exact fill?
faqs.answer: No. It provides a repeatable capacity input, but braid thickness, winding tension, and the reel's published capacity can affect the real fill. Stop at the reel manufacturer's fill level.

berkley-x5-braid.quickSummary: Berkley X5 is a five-carrier PE braid marketed for fishing around cover. The selected pound test identifies a specific catalog entry, while its published diameter drives the capacity estimate. Use this page to plan a full braid spool or a working section above backing.
berkley-x5-braid.suitabilitySummary: X5 can be considered for braid applications around vegetation and cover where the line strength, lure, and tackle are matched to the job. A cover-focused description does not make every X5 strength a heavy-cover recommendation. The lightest diameters still require a suitable reel and careful line handling.
berkley-x5-braid.chartNote: Strength and retail length are taken from US product options; diameters are matched using the same official product codes. Millimeter values are converted from the published inch diameter. Only resolved combinations are included.
strengthGuide: The 8-15 lb entries are the lightest choices shown. Treat them as fine braid, not heavy-cover line simply because the X5 family is marketed for cover. Check the rod and intended presentation before deciding on a strength.

The 20-40 lb entries span different diameters for general and stronger braid setups. A baitcaster may be easier to manage with a less delicate diameter, but lure weight, cover, and spool behavior should decide the choice.

The 50-80 lb entries belong to heavier applications that justify them. More breaking strength does not automatically improve casting or make a light rod suitable for dense cover. The capacity tool shows fit, not a blanket fishing recommendation.

spoolingGuide.title: Choose a useful working length
spoolingGuide.text: Plan enough braid for your normal casts, expected runs, and a reserve for cutting back damaged line. Backing can make up the remaining spool space without buying braid for the entire spool.

spoolingGuide.title: Check the connection
spoolingGuide.text: Use a connection appropriate to the braid and backing diameters, seat it carefully, and keep it below the normal working section. A tight, bulky knot can affect how the first braid wraps lie.

spoolingGuide.title: Inspect after contact
spoolingGuide.text: A cover-oriented braid still needs inspection. Check for damage after rubbing vegetation stems, wood, or rough structure, and cut back compromised line instead of relying on the strength label.

faqs.question: Is X5 a four-strand braid?
faqs.answer: No. Berkley describes X5 as a five-carrier PE braid. It is a different construction from its nine-carrier X9 model.

faqs.question: Does X5 hold less line than X9 at the same pound test?
faqs.answer: Use the listed diameters for the exact entries. Where two entries have the same diameter, the mathematical capacity estimate is the same; their construction or handling can still differ.

faqs.question: Can I put the whole 164-yard package on my reel?
faqs.answer: Only if your selected reel has enough estimated space at that diameter. Use a capacity calculation first, and stop at the correct fill level. If the package does not fill the reel, the backing mode can estimate what is needed beneath it.

spoolingGuide.title: Read JFS on the package

spoolingGuide.title: Check FC, 90m and SKU

shimano-kairiki-8.suitabilityTitle: Is Kairiki 8 right for your setup?
shimano-kairiki-8.suitabilitySummary: Consider this bulk version when you maintain several reels or need repeat fills from one supply. A multicolor mainline can help track paid-out line, while Mantis Green provides a single-color choice. Carrier count and coating descriptions are not a substitute for matching strength, reserve and reel capacity to your fishing.
strengthGuide: The exact Australian 20 lb bulk diameter is .20 mm; 30 lb is .23 mm. These values belong to the SKE3000 SKU family, not an assumed universal Kairiki chart.

spoolingGuide.title: Allocate a bulk supply
spoolingGuide.text: 3,000 meters converts to approximately 3,280.84 yards. Choose a working length and reserve for each reel before deciding how many fills the supply will provide.

spoolingGuide.title: Keep an allowance for losses
spoolingGuide.text: Plan for future reties and damaged line removal, especially when dividing one bulk spool across several reels. A nominally exact division leaves no reserve for those losses.

spoolingGuide.title: Read the Australian code
spoolingGuide.text: The verified 20 lb codes are SKE300020G and SKE300020M. Shorter filler packages and other regions need their own diameter evidence; a similar name is not enough.

faqs.question: Does this cover the 150m filler spool?

faqs.question: Is Kairiki 8 the same as Kairiki 8+?
faqs.answer: No. The plus model is a separate product identity. This page uses the standard Kairiki 8 bulk SKU range.

faqs.question: Can I divide a bulk spool equally among reels?
faqs.answer: Only after checking each reel and desired working length. Different spool sizes and line diameters need different amounts, and future trimming requires reserve.

spoolingGuide.title: Separate title strength from table labels

spoolingGuide.title: Keep the mainline and leader distinct
spoolingGuide.text: Choose terminal leader material and its connection independently. The short leader section is not the mainline used in the capacity calculation.

faqs.answer: No. It is the manufacturer's explicit average-strength label. This guide does not rename it or reuse an old 40 lb row.

shimano-ocea-ex-fluorocarbon-leader.suitabilityTitle: Is Ocea EX Fluorocarbon Leader right for your setup?
shimano-ocea-ex-fluorocarbon-leader.suitabilitySummary: Ocea EX is a terminal fluorocarbon option for joining to your mainline, with a layered structure and a broad range of diameters. strengthGuide: The 20 lb SKU is .377 mm, 30 lb is .476 mm, 40 lb is .577 mm, and 50 lb is .628 mm. Do not substitute a generic fluorocarbon diameter chart.
Select leader size with knot bulk and guide clearance in mind. A longer leader puts the connection through the guides more often; no universal knot-length recommendation is implied here.
If braid is on the reel, its diameter controls the working capacity. A short Ocea EX leader does not justify using the leader's strength as the braid rating.

spoolingGuide.title: Plan individual leader lengths
spoolingGuide.text: Decide how much terminal material your rig needs and allow additional material for tying and future reties. The package length is the total supply; it is not the required length of one leader.

spoolingGuide.title: Match the package to the strength
spoolingGuide.text: The verified 4-100 lb entries use 50-meter spools. The 130 lb entry uses 20 meters. In yard units these are approximately 54.68 and 21.87 yards, not additional retail options.

spoolingGuide.title: Check the connection after contact
spoolingGuide.text: Inspect the leader and knot after rubbing against structure or landing a fish. Replace compromised material before continuing, and test that the connection clears the guides if it passes through them.

faqs.question: Is Ocea EX the same as Ocea 8?
faqs.answer: No. Ocea EX Fluoro Leader is fluorocarbon leader material; Ocea 8 is braided mainline.

faqs.question: Why is 130 lb sold in a shorter length?
faqs.answer: The official table lists a 20-meter package at 130 lb. This guide reports that package without inferring an unavailable 50-meter option.

faqs.question: Should I use leader strength to calculate braid capacity?
faqs.answer: No. Use the braid actually wound on the reel. A terminal Ocea EX section does not change that mainline into fluorocarbon or give it the leader strength label.

strengthGuide: Choose the leader for the terminal connection, cover, lure, and knot requirements. The leader's pound-test label does not determine how much braid fits on the reel.

UK Grand Max tippet uses different strength labels and package lengths. Do not merge it with this US-import JDM collection.

spoolingGuide.title: Treat 60 meters as leader supply

spoolingGuide.title: Keep nearby labels distinct
spoolingGuide.text: Label each spool by the actual test and diameter. The 17, 19, 24 and 27 lb options are not interchangeable with conventional 15, 20, 25 or 30 lb labels.

spoolingGuide.title: Protect the remaining material
spoolingGuide.text: Keep the free end controlled on the compact spool and separate damaged material from the unused supply. Check the terminal section and connection after abrasion or a hard pull.

faqs.question: Should Grand Max fill the reel?
faqs.answer: This product is documented as leader/tippet material. Calculate the working spool with the actual main line, then select Grand Max for the terminal section.

faqs.question: Can 19 lb be renamed 20 lb?
faqs.answer: No. 19 lb is the exact published US variant label, SKU 19GM66. A nearby familiar pound test is a different identity.

spro-finesse-braid-8x.metaDescription: Check verified SPRO Finesse Braid 8X diameters and strength-specific packages. Plan a full reel fill or a working length over backing with the exact line diameter.
spro-finesse-braid-8x.quickSummary: Finesse Braid 8X is SPRO's 6-16 lb finesse braid in 150 m packages, labeled 164 yards. Lime Green and Flash Pink are separate color variants. The diameter chart here is read from the actual Lime Green package labels, not calculated from their numbered line-size labels.
spro-finesse-braid-8x.construction: Japanese eight-strand braid, positioned by SPRO as soft and limp for finesse fishing
spro-finesse-braid-8x.suitabilityTitle: Is Finesse Braid 8X right for your setup?
spro-finesse-braid-8x.suitabilitySummary: This is a finesse-oriented mainline for anglers who want braid on a lighter setup and may add a short leader. SPRO emphasizes limp handling and offers a visible Lime Green color. The very thin 6 lb size can yield a high mathematical capacity on an ordinary spinning reel, making a planned working section and backing more useful than an automatic full-braid fill.
strengthGuide: The package labels list 6 lb at 0.10 mm, 8 lb at 0.13 mm and 10 lb at 0.16 mm. These are printed physical diameters, not a PE-number conversion.
The 12, 14 and 16 lb options are 0.18, 0.20 and 0.22 mm. Match the rod and leader connection to the exact size instead of assuming all finesse braids share a diameter.
This 6-16 lb family is not Bronzeye Braid for heavy-cover frogging. A technique name is not a reason to stretch a light-line setup beyond the rod or drag requirements.

spoolingGuide.title: Plan with the package label
spoolingGuide.text: Each verified Lime Green filler is 150 m, also labeled 164 yd. Select a working length within that supply and allow extra line for trimming and runs.

spoolingGuide.title: Give thin braid a secure base
spoolingGuide.text: Use the reel manufacturer's approved braid attachment and maintain firm, even tension. A thin line can fit in large quantities; unused volume can be occupied by sound backing.

spoolingGuide.title: Choose the leader separately
spoolingGuide.text: A short leader at the lure end can be replaced without replacing the whole braid fill. Its strength should suit the cover and presentation; it need not simply copy the braid pound label.

faqs.question: How much Finesse Braid 8X will fit my reel?
faqs.answer: Use the exact strength and the reel's published capacity. Pound test is not a fixed diameter, so equal-strength products can produce different fill estimates.

spro-essential-bronzeye-8x.quickSummary: Essential Bronzeye 8X is the product SPRO names Bronzeye Braid 8X and identifies as Essential Series. It is positioned for frogging and flipping, with 40, 50, 60 and 80 lb Moss Green options in 150 m / 164 yd packages.
spro-essential-bronzeye-8x.construction: Japanese eight-strand braid in SPRO's Essential Series; Moss Green
spro-essential-bronzeye-8x.suitabilityTitle: Is Essential Bronzeye 8X right for your setup?
spro-essential-bronzeye-8x.suitabilitySummary: Bronzeye is a candidate for a suitable heavy-cover casting setup, not a general finesse braid. Pick the frog or flipping presentation, rod power and reel first. Its 40-80 lb range calls for deliberate drag and hook-setting judgment; the printed strength does not establish the safe load for the rod or reel.
strengthGuide: The 40 and 50 lb package labels show 0.28 and 0.315 mm. Even within the same Bronzeye family, moving up changes how much fits the spool.
The 60 and 80 lb labels show 0.35 and 0.42 mm. Check capacity and rod rating before selecting the heavier size for vegetation or cover.
SPRO does not list a 65 lb Bronzeye option in these variants. Do not relabel 60 lb as 65 lb to match another brand's range.

spoolingGuide.title: Make a casting-length plan
spoolingGuide.text: Start with casts, a reserve for fighting fish and enough line for retying. A 164-yard filler may leave surplus on a compact casting reel; do not overfill to use it all.

spoolingGuide.title: Keep a firm braid bed
spoolingGuide.text: Follow the reel's braid attachment instructions and wind under even tension. After a heavy load, check that line has not buried into a loosely wound lower layer.

spoolingGuide.title: Consider the connection for the cover
spoolingGuide.text: Straight braid and braid with a leader are different rigging choices. Choose for the lure and contact surfaces; neither choice changes the physical Bronzeye diameter used for capacity.

spro-depth-control-8x.quickSummary: Depth Control 8X is SPRO's metered ocean braid for high-speed and slow-pitch jigging. The official page specifies color coding every 10 m. Verified 30-80 lb packages include 300 m fillers and 3,000 m bulk spools.
spro-depth-control-8x.construction: Eight-strand ocean-fishing braid with pitch marks and color changes every 10 m
spro-depth-control-8x.suitabilityTitle: Is Depth Control 8X right for your setup?
spro-depth-control-8x.suitabilitySummary: This line is aimed at anglers who need a repeatable indication of line paid out when jigging. Metered line tracks deployment length, not guaranteed vertical lure depth: current, boat drift and line angle still matter. Choose enough working braid for the intended water depth and fish runs before using any backing.
strengthGuide: The 30 and 40 lb labels are 0.24 and 0.28 mm. A smaller diameter can change capacity substantially, but strength choice still needs to suit jig weight, drag and target fish.
The 50, 60 and 80 lb labels are 0.315, 0.35 and 0.42 mm. Check the selected reel's real capacity rather than assuming a 300 m filler fits every offshore spool.
The 2026 catalog describes additional very heavy sizes. They are not added here without corresponding reviewed diameter evidence and current package identity.

spoolingGuide.title: Start with depth and reserve
spoolingGuide.text: Allow for deployment beyond the vertical water depth when the line is angled, plus fish runs and future trimming. Backing should remain below the working braid throughout that plan.

spoolingGuide.title: Count marks, not assumed depth
spoolingGuide.text: SPRO specifies color changes every 10 m. Count them as line-out information; do not treat each color as proof the jig is exactly 10 m deeper.

spoolingGuide.title: Match 300 m or bulk to the reel
spoolingGuide.text: The filler package is labeled 300 m / 328 yd. The 3,000 m offering is bulk supply and should be divided by actual fill needs, not guessed from the number of reels.

yo-zuri-hybrid-ice-line.construction: Nylon/fluorocarbon copolymer formulated and packaged as Hybrid Ice Line
yo-zuri-hybrid-ice-line.suitabilityTitle: Is Hybrid Ice Line right for your setup?
yo-zuri-hybrid-ice-line.suitabilitySummary: Hybrid Ice is a light-line option for an ice reel where depth, presentation and reserve determine the required working supply. Its 55-yard package should not be treated as a full-spool guarantee. Plan for the deepest deployment, fish movement and trimming; a short supply is less forgiving when the water is deep.
strengthGuide: The 1 and 2 lb sizes are published at 0.127 and 0.152 mm. Such light labels call for appropriately light tackle, gentle handling and a checked knot rather than reliance on a capacity result.
The 3-6 lb group runs through 0.170, 0.203, 0.220 and 0.254 mm. The ordinary Hybrid 4 lb chart is thicker, so do not use it for this Ice package.
Choose strength for the lure, hook and likely fish; then check depth plus reserve against 55 yards. The smallest diameter is not automatically the best choice.

spoolingGuide.title: Budget for the whole deployment
spoolingGuide.text: Enter enough working line for water depth and a realistic reserve. Backing can fill a deep spool, but it does not extend the 55 yards of Hybrid Ice available to fish.

spoolingGuide.title: Use a suitable small reel
spoolingGuide.text: A small ice or light spinning reel may be a practical match. If the reel holds much more than 55 yards, plan the backing connection so it remains below normal deployment.

spoolingGuide.title: Check the cold-weather working section
spoolingGuide.text: Inspect line near the lure and any contact points, including the ice edge. Replace visibly damaged line and retie as needed; the manufacturer's waterproof positioning does not remove mechanical wear.

spiderwire-ultracast-braid.seoTitle: SpiderWire Ultracast 8 lb Diameter & Capacity Guide | ReelCalc
spiderwire-ultracast-braid.metaDescription: Plan an 8 lb SpiderWire Ultracast Inshore Camo setup using its labeled diameter and 164-yard package. Estimate reel capacity, working braid and mono backing.
spiderwire-ultracast-braid.quickSummary: Ultracast is an eight-fiber PE braid. This guide is limited to the labeled 8 lb Inshore Camo package, not the full Ultracast range. Its 164-yard spool gives you a defined amount of working braid to plan around; a large capacity estimate does not mean you need to fill the entire reel with it.
spiderwire-ultracast-braid.suitabilityTitle: A thin working line, with a specific label
spiderwire-ultracast-braid.suitabilitySummary: Consider this 8 lb variant only where the rod, lure and fishing conditions suit light braid. A spinning-reel setup with a deliberately chosen working length is a sensible planning example. Inshore Camo is a color name, not proof that this strength suits every inshore fishery. The unusually small published diameter makes backing calculations sensitive to the label and to real-world packing, so finish by checking the reel's recommended fill level.
strengthGuide: Match the 8 lb test rating to the rod, lure and likely loads first. Do not select it solely because the small published diameter produces a large capacity estimate.
The package also prints a maximum-break figure. That is a different label field, not a substitute for the 8 lb test rating and not an instruction to use a heavier drag setting.
Only this labeled variant is charted here. Use separately verified data for stronger Ultracast, another color formulation, or the older Ultimate Braid and Invisibraid products.
spiderwire-ultracast-braid.bestFit: A light spinning setup where the angler has already selected 8 lb braid and wants a measured working section over backing. Keep enough reserve for the longest cast, fish runs and line removed through use.
spiderwire-ultracast-braid.tradeoffTitle: Published diameter is not a fill guarantee
spiderwire-ultracast-braid.tradeoff: Braid can pack differently with tension and spool geometry. With such a small listed diameter, an apparent surplus of reel capacity should be handled with a backing plan, not a promise that an exact calculated length will fit in practice.
spiderwire-ultracast-braid.reviewNote: This is a specification-based guide. No casting-distance, abrasion or handling performance was independently tested.
spiderwire-ultracast-braid.chartNote: One verified package only: 8 lb Inshore Camo, labeled 164 yd / 150 m. Other Ultracast strengths are intentionally absent because their physical diameters and matching packages were not verified from the current manufacturer's evidence.
spiderwire-ultracast-braid.diameterNote: The package independently prints 0.0035 in and 0.09 mm. These agree within rounding; the inch figure is the calculation input. They are manufacturer label values, not ReelCalc measurements.
spiderwire-ultracast-braid.exampleBackingLabel: Berkley Trilene Big Game 10 lb mono (0.012 in)
spiderwire-ultracast-braid.sourceNote: Checked September 13, 2026. The current US Ultracast page links the Inshore Camo package image used for this single row and lists the matching test strength and package length. The image filename dates the artwork to 2019. No claim of current stock, revised packaging or full-range verification is made.

spoolingGuide.title: Budget from the 164-yard package
spoolingGuide.text: Start with your required working length, leaving room for trimming and future losses. The examples use 125 or 150 yards from one package, not a promise that either length suits every fishery.

spoolingGuide.title: Fill the remaining volume underneath
spoolingGuide.text: Choose the exact reel before estimating mono backing. Follow its instructions for attaching braid; a smooth arbor may need an approved anti-slip attachment or a mono base. Backing length is a volume calculation, not a matching pound-test rule.

spoolingGuide.title: Treat the leader separately
spoolingGuide.text: Choose any lure-end leader for the presentation and contact hazards. It is not the backing beneath the braid, and its test rating need not copy the braid label. A long topshot needs a separate allowance for spool space.

spoolingGuide.title: Check the final fill
spoolingGuide.text: Wind with controlled, even tension and stop at the reel manufacturer's specified clearance. Correct the backing amount if the actual fill differs from the estimate; do not force all the planned line onto an overfull spool.

spiderwire-ultracast-braid.reelcalcNote: Estimate capacity with the labeled inch diameter, then compare the working length with this specific retail package.

manufacturerFacts.text: The inspected Inshore Camo label identifies an 8 lb test, 164-yard / 150-meter package.

manufacturerFacts.label: Published construction

manufacturerFacts.text: SpiderWire attributes improved abrasion performance to its cold-fusion process. That comparison has not been independently tested here.

setupComparison.title: Working braid or a full braid fill?
setupComparison.leftText: Useful when your chosen working length is shorter than the reel's estimated full-braid capacity. It allocates the package to fishing line above a calculated mono base.
setupComparison.rightText: May require more than one package with this small published diameter. Choose it because the fishing needs that reserve, not because a capacity estimate suggests unused space must contain more braid.

productGuidance: Match Ultracast x8, Inshore Camo and the 8 lb test label before using this row.

faqs.question: Why does this Ultracast chart show only 8 lb?
faqs.answer: The currently displayed Inshore Camo package provides a readable test rating, both diameters and a matching length. Other strengths appear in the manufacturer's selector, but that alone does not verify their physical diameters or package combinations.

faqs.question: Is the 22 lb maximum-break marking another strength?
faqs.answer: No. On the inspected package, 8 lb is the test label and 22 lb is a separate maximum-break claim. This chart uses the test label and does not create a 22 lb variant.

faqs.question: Does one package fill my reel?
faqs.answer: That depends on the exact reel and the actual packing. Compare its estimated capacity with your required working length; use backing when a suitable working section is shorter than a full fill.

faqs.question: Can I use this diameter for Invisibraid or Ultimate Braid?
faqs.answer: No. The evidence here identifies the Inshore Camo Ultracast x8 package. Similar names, old catalog groupings and matching pound-test labels do not establish identical physical diameters.

faqs.question: Why can the calculated capacity look unusually large?
faqs.answer: The package lists a very small diameter. Capacity estimates depend strongly on that input, while actual braid packing also depends on winding tension and spool shape. Treat the result as a planning estimate and verify the final fill.

cortland-master-braid.seoTitle: Cortland Master Braid Diameter Chart & Reel Capacity | ReelCalc
cortland-master-braid.metaDescription: Compare verified Cortland Master Braid diameters and strength-specific spool lengths, estimate reel capacity, and plan a full fill or a working section over backing.
cortland-master-braid.quickSummary: Cortland Master Braid changes construction with strength: the official chart uses four carriers through 40 lb, six at 50-65 lb, eight at 80 lb and twelve at 100-200 lb. This package evidence covers the White color only, not Premium Metered or discontinued-color stock.
cortland-master-braid.construction: Spectra braid with size-specific 4-12 carrier construction; FiberTech protection and ColorLast
cortland-master-braid.suitabilityTitle: Is Master Braid right for your setup?
cortland-master-braid.suitabilitySummary: Master Braid is a useful comparison for spinning, baitcasting or conventional setups, all of which Cortland includes in its positioning. The current white version prioritizes visible line tracking. Its carrier count and diameter both depend on the selected strength, so describing every Master Braid as an eight-carrier line would misrepresent the product.
strengthGuide: The 5, 8 and 10 lb rows use four carriers and diameters of 0.004, 0.005 and 0.006 inch. Select these for appropriately light tackle rather than using minimum diameter as the only way to maximize capacity.
The 15-40 lb strengths remain four-carrier, with 20 lb at 0.010 inch and 30 lb at 0.012 inch. Compare the true diameters with other braids, not the chart's mono-equivalent strength column.

Construction changes to six carriers at 50/65 lb, eight at 80 lb and twelve at 100 lb and above. The heavy variants also have different retail lengths; they are not ordinary small-reel recommendations.

spoolingGuide.title: Match white packages to the chosen strength
spoolingGuide.text: White has verified 150- and 300-yard packages through 80 lb. The 100 and 130 lb retail choice begins at 200 yards, while the current 200 lb variant evidence uses 1200 and 2500 yards. Do not apply all page-wide lengths to every strength.

spoolingGuide.title: Use the appropriate braid attachment
spoolingGuide.text: Secure the arbor using the reel maker's approved method or a suitable mono base. FiberTech protection and ColorLast do not establish that an unapproved knot on a smooth arbor will grip.

spoolingGuide.title: Treat other Master Braid variants separately
spoolingGuide.text: Premium Metered, other colors and DQ-labeled packages have their own product variants. This White evidence set does not promise every color is offered at the same strength and length.

setupComparison.title: Planning a Master Braid setup
setupComparison.leftText: Choose a visible working section long enough for casts, runs and trimming; backing occupies unused spool space.
setupComparison.rightText: Use its exact diameter for a continuous braid fill with a reel-approved attachment; carrier count is specific to strength.

productGuidance: White has verified 150- and 300-yard packages through 80 lb. The 100 and 130 lb retail choice begins at 200 yards, while the current 200 lb variant evidence uses 1200 and 2500 yards. Do not apply all page-wide lengths to every strength.
Secure the arbor using the reel maker's approved method or a suitable mono base. FiberTech protection and ColorLast do not establish that an unapproved knot on a smooth arbor will grip.
Premium Metered, other colors and DQ-labeled packages have their own product variants. This White evidence set does not promise every color is offered at the same strength and length.
cortland-master-braid.recommendationIntro: Match the starting range to an offered Master Braid strength, then check diameter, rod rating, lure and cover. The recommendation is not a promise that every size will handle well on your reel.

faqs.question: Is all Master Braid eight-carrier?
faqs.answer: No. Cortland's chart specifies four, six, eight or twelve carriers by strength. In the verified range only 80 lb uses eight carriers.

faqs.question: Can I use mono equivalent as the braid diameter?
faqs.answer: No. The official chart has separate inch and millimeter diameter columns. Mono equivalent is a comparison label, not a physical diameter measurement.

faqs.question: Are all Master Braid spool lengths available at every strength?
faqs.answer: No. This guide matches White product variants to the corresponding strengths and keeps the heavy 200-yard and bulk-only combinations separate.

faqs.question: How much Master Braid fits my reel?
faqs.answer: Use the selected Master Braid diameter with your reel's published capacity. Pound test is a product strength label, not a universal diameter. Stop filling at the reel manufacturer's recommended level.

faqs.question: Does Master Braid require backing?
faqs.answer: Use the reel manufacturer's approved braid attachment method. On a smooth arbor, a sound mono base can provide grip; additional backing can reduce the braid needed for a planned working length.

cortland-fluorocarbon-leader.quickSummary: Cortland Fluorocarbon Leader Material is dedicated terminal material, separate from XTR Leader and Ultra Premium Top Secret Tippet. This guide includes 16 chart-supported strengths from 6 to 200 lb, with 30- and 100-yard packages. The 50-lb row is excluded because the manufacturer photo has a conflicting diameter pair.
cortland-fluorocarbon-leader.suitabilitySummary: Use the ordinary Fluorocarbon Leader Material identity when choosing a bite or terminal section. It is not the XTR formulation or the X-rated Ultra Premium tippet system. Current sale-feed variants are limited, but the product's complete size/length chart remains evidence of the documented range, not a live-stock promise.
strengthGuide: The ordinary leader chart lists 6, 8, 10 and 12 lb at 0.007, 0.009, 0.011 and 0.012 inch. Choose by the terminal presentation and cover, not the capacity rating printed on a reel.
The next official step is 16 lb at 0.014 inch. The catalog's 15 lb leader has no matching source row and must stay held; it cannot inherit the 16 lb identity.

The included chart extends to 200 lb for heavy terminal applications, with a gap at the held 50-lb strength. The presence of those rows is not a small-tackle recommendation, a knot-strength guarantee or permission to calculate a reel full of leader stock.

spoolingGuide.title: Plan replacement sections
spoolingGuide.text: Select the leader's finished length, add knot allowance, then budget the number of leaders and trimming reserve from a 30- or 100-yard package. Do not turn package yardage into a recommended leader length.

spoolingGuide.title: Separate documented range from stock
spoolingGuide.text: The official table links both package lengths to each included strength; 50 lb is held out because of conflicting manufacturer diameter evidence. Only three variants remain in the saved sale feed. This guide cites the table for range and does not claim that every combination can currently be ordered.

spoolingGuide.title: Use the exact Cortland family
spoolingGuide.text: Keep ordinary Fluorocarbon Leader Material distinct from XTR Leader and Top Secret/Ultra Premium Tippet. Their formulation names, strength labels and diameters must not be swapped.

faqs.question: Why is 50 lb excluded?
faqs.answer: The source chart prints 0.025 inch, which converts to 0.635 mm. The rear spool in the manufacturer photo prints 0.025 inch / 0.66 mm, with its 50-lb text partly hidden. The competing claims remain unresolved, so no 50-lb row or corrected diameter is supplied.

gamma-touch-fluorocarbon.seoTitle: Gamma Touch Fluorocarbon Diameter Chart & Reel Capacity | ReelCalc
gamma-touch-fluorocarbon.metaDescription: Compare verified Gamma Touch Fluorocarbon diameters and strength-specific spool lengths, estimate reel capacity, and plan a full fill or a working section over backing.
gamma-touch-fluorocarbon.quickSummary: Touch is Gamma's finesse-focused fluorocarbon, with 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8 and 9 lb U.S. sizes. The manufacturer specifically positions it for drop-shot techniques. Its half-thousandth-inch diameter steps matter: 7 lb is 0.0085 inch, not a rounded generic 0.009-inch line.
gamma-touch-fluorocarbon.suitabilityTitle: Is Touch Fluorocarbon right for your setup?
gamma-touch-fluorocarbon.suitabilitySummary: Touch is the relevant Gamma option when small-diameter fluorocarbon and finesse presentations drive the choice. It stops at 9 lb rather than extending into Edge's heavier strengths. That narrower range can simplify a light spinning setup, but using the thinnest option only to increase capacity can leave too little margin for cover and drag. Gamma's sensitivity and flexibility claims are not independent test results.
strengthGuide: The 2-5 lb sizes measure 0.0045-0.0075 inch. Match these light lines to a suitable rod, carefully set drag and the actual cover; they are not substitutes for heavier line simply because a fish has been landed on them before.
The next offered size after 5 lb is 7 lb. There is no verified 6 lb Touch row in this range, so do not borrow 6 lb Edge's diameter or relabel the 7 lb Touch SKU.

The 7, 8 and 9 lb steps are 0.0085, 0.0095 and 0.0105 inch. Keep the fourth decimal for capacity calculations even if a display rounds the chart; the 9 lb size is not a universal heavy-cover recommendation.

spoolingGuide.title: Choose the refill for more working line
spoolingGuide.text: The 100-yard filler is useful for a planned short working section; a verified 200-yard refill gives more room for a full fill or reserve. Keep package length tied to its matching table and SKU.

spoolingGuide.title: Keep a buried knot out of a finesse cast
spoolingGuide.text: A short fresh Touch section over backing can save line, but measure enough for your longest cast plus trimming and runs. Do not let a small package dictate a working length that exposes the connection during normal use.

spoolingGuide.title: Retain the exact diameter
spoolingGuide.text: Touch's 0.0005-inch increments are part of the manufacturer specification. Use the exact stored figure when comparing it with Edge or another fluorocarbon; a rounded chart value is for display only.
